She threatens him: he is polite and sad about it, like a son disappointed in a parent.
She asks about Rose: he grows interested and dangerous; he knows the girl is special.
suggestions: Why did you do it?
Take off your glasses.
What do you want with Rose?

exits.5.2a.UNMAKE: Aurie unmakes him, back into sand.
exits.5.2a.REMAKE: Aurie orders him home to the Dreaming, to be remade better.

GLASSES.when: She makes him take off his glasses.
GLASSES.ripple: Behind the dark lenses, two small mouths smile at her.

choices.text: You were a mistake. I unmake you.

aftermath.text: Aurie raises her hand. The Corinthian comes apart into sand, and is gone.
Only a small white skull is left on the carpet. Where its eyes should be, two tiny rows of teeth.
Then Aurie turns to the killers in their chairs, and makes every one of them see exactly what they are.

choices.text: Come home. I'll make you better.

aftermath.text: The Corinthian bows. His shape loosens into sand, and drifts away toward the Dreaming.
Lucienne will lock that sand away until Aurie is ready to shape him again.
Then Aurie turns to the killers in their chairs, and makes every one of them see exactly what they are.

choices.text: Go, then. You're not my concern.

aftermath.text: The Corinthian smiles, puts his glasses back on, and walks out into the night.
Somewhere in the Dreaming, a door that should be shut swings quietly open.

5.2b.title: The Vortex
5.2b.recap: Rose Walker turned out to be a dream vortex, tearing the Dreaming apart.

beats.text: Rose has found her brother. Tonight she sleeps in an old boarding house in Florida.
She dreams. And the walls between the dreams of everyone in the house come down.
Every dreamer falls into one shared dream, and the shared dream begins to swallow the Dreaming.
Lucienne's library is coming apart, page by page. Rose Walker is a vortex.
Aurie walks into the heart of the storm, and every torn page in the air turns to look at her.
Once in a great many ages, a vortex is born. If she is not stopped, every dreaming mind will be torn apart.
Aurie finds her at the centre of it, small and terrified.

canon: Rose Walker is a twenty-year-old American woman. She did not ask to be a vortex and does not understand what is happening. She thought she was only dreaming.

A dream vortex breaks the walls between dreams. If it is not stopped, the Dreaming collapses and with it every dreaming mind in the world. The only known way to stop a vortex is for Dream to take her life.
Rose has just found her little brother Jed after months of searching. She is kind, brave, and frightened, and she understands faster than Aurie expects.
Rose's grandmother is Unity Kincaid, the girl who slept through Aurie's captivity; Rose does not know that Unity is her grandmother.
conversation.opening: You're the lady from my dreams, aren't you? Please. Tell me what's happening. Everything's falling apart, and I think it's because of me.
possibilities: She tells Rose the truth: Rose takes it in, cries, then asks if there is any other way.
She comforts her: Rose holds on to that, and asks her to be honest anyway.
She asks about Jed: Rose's face lights up, and that makes it worse.
She says nothing: Rose begs her to say something, anything.
suggestions: It isn't your fault, Rose.
Tell me about your brother.
Is there another way?

exits.5.2b.KILL: Aurie decides she must take Rose's life to save the Dreaming.
exits.5.2b.WAIT: Aurie refuses to kill Rose yet, and searches for another way while the Dreaming tears.

ROSE_COMFORTED.when: She comforts Rose honestly, or tells her it is not her fault.

choices.text: I'm sorry, Rose. It has to be me who ends this.

aftermath.text: Aurie raises her hand. Rose does not run. She only closes her eyes.
And a voice behind them says: wait.

choices.text: No. Not you. There has to be another way.

aftermath.text: Aurie lowers her hand. Around them, the library tears, shelf by shelf.
And a voice behind them says: there is.

5.2c.title: Unity
5.2c.recap: Unity Kincaid, Rose's grandmother, took the vortex into herself and died in Rose's place.

beats.text: An old woman stands in the dream. She is eighty-five, in a pale blue dressing gown, and she is smiling.
Unity Kincaid. The girl who fell asleep in 1916, while Aurie was in the glass, and slept for seventy years.
Unity is Rose's great-grandmother. The vortex was born in Unity, seventy years ago, while she slept. With no Dream to tend it, it passed down her line to Rose.
Aurie spoke with her once, in her dream, when she was ten.
Long ago, in that dream, Aurie promised the girl she would not be forgotten. Unity remembers.

canon: Unity Kincaid is about eighty-five and dying in a nursing home; she is here in the dream. She caught the sleeping sickness in 1916 while Aurie was imprisoned, and slept for seventy years.
While she slept, someone visited her dreams and she became pregnant. Her daughter's child is Rose. Unity has only just understood all of this.
Unity was meant to be the vortex, not Rose. Because Aurie was imprisoned, it passed to Rose. Unity can take it back into herself, and she will die, gently, in Rose's place. She is at peace with it.
The one who visited her dreams and planned all this was Desire, Aurie's own sibling, who hoped Aurie would kill her own family's blood. Unity says it was 'someone golden, perfumed, smiling'.
conversation.opening: It should have been me, dear. I was meant to be the vortex. I've had a long life, mostly asleep. Let me give Rose the rest of hers.
possibilities: She thanks Unity: Unity says there's nothing to thank, it's only putting things back where they belong.
She asks who the father of Unity's child was: Unity describes someone golden and perfumed who smiled in her dreams; Aurie knows exactly who that is.
She tries to stop her: Unity is gently firm, and asks Aurie to let an old woman be brave.
She remembers their talk in 1916: Unity laughs; she remembers the lady in the glass, and any promise Aurie made her (flag UNITY_PROMISE).
suggestions: Who visited your dreams?
You were the girl who couldn't wake.
Are you afraid?

exits.5.2c.LET: Aurie accepts Unity's gift and lets her take the vortex.

triggers.player: thank you|go on|do it|let her|i understand|goodbye|very well|be at peace

NAMED_DESIRE.when: Aurie realises, or Unity's description shows, that Desire was behind it all.
NAMED_DESIRE.ripple: Somewhere very far away, Desire stops smiling.

echo.text: Dream learned that Desire planted the vortex in her own family's blood, to make her kill it.

choices.text: Thank you, Unity.

aftermath.text: Unity takes Rose's hand. The light of the vortex flows out of the girl and into the old woman.
Unity smiles, and closes her eyes, and is gone. Death is waiting for her, kindly.
The walls of the dreams close again. Rose wakes in Florida, alive, with her brother asleep in the next room.
Rose will never forget that the lady from her dreams raised a hand to kill her.

5.2d.title: Desire's Threshold
5.2d.recap: Aurie confronted Desire, who had planned the vortex to make her kill her own kin.

beats.text: Aurie does not go home. There is one visit she owes first.
Desire lives in a vast statue of itself, shaped like a heart. Aurie walks straight in.
Desire made the vortex happen. It hoped Aurie would kill a child of her own family, and be destroyed for it.
Desire is lounging on a velvet couch, and does not pretend to be surprised.
Aurie stands in the doorway of its red room and does not sit.

canon: Desire, Aurie's sibling, visited Unity Kincaid's dreams in 1916 and fathered her child, so that the vortex would pass to Unity's family. Desire hoped Aurie would kill Rose, her own kin, and bring the Kindly Ones down on herself.
Desire denies nothing directly and enjoys the conversation. It never apologises.
Aurie can threaten Desire, or warn it once and leave. Either way, the plan has failed and Desire knows it.
conversation.opening: Sister. You look so serious. Did something happen? You didn't kill the girl. How very unlike you.
possibilities: She accuses Desire: Desire smiles and says it only wanted to see what she would do.
She asks why: Desire says because she is always so sure of herself, and someone ought to test that.
She is calm: that unsettles Desire more than anger.
suggestions: You wanted me to kill her.
Why do you hate me?

exits.5.2d.WARN: Aurie warns Desire, once, and leaves.

choices.text: Touch my family again and I will end you.

aftermath.text: For one moment, Desire looks afraid. Then the smile returns, a little thinner than before.

choices.text: This is your only warning.

aftermath.text: Aurie leaves. Behind her, Desire laughs, and the laugh goes on a little too long.

5.3.title: Men of Good Fortune
5.3.recap: In 1389 Death granted Hob Gadling his wish never to die, and Aurie agreed to meet him once every hundred years.

beats.text: There is one more appointment Aurie keeps. She has kept it every hundred years for six centuries.
Aurie and her sister Death sit in the corner of a smoky London tavern, watching the living.
A loud young man named Hob Gadling is telling his friends that dying is a mug's game. He doesn't intend to do it.
Death laughs. She grants it, for her sister's sake, to see what happens.
Aurie walks over to his table. Meet me here in a hundred years, she tells him, and tell me if you still think so.
Hob is waiting. He is rich now, and he still loves every day of it.
A young writer in the corner, Will Shaxberd, begs Aurie for the gift of telling stories. She makes him a bargain.
Hob has lost everything, his money, his wife, his son. He still does not want to die.
Hob is rich again, in a powdered wig. He has made his money from ships that carry slaves.

choices.text: It is a poor thing, Hob, to be a slaver.

aftermath.text: Hob goes red, and blusters, and does not forget it. He sells the ships before the next century comes.

choices.text: (Say nothing.)

aftermath.text: Aurie says nothing. Hob laughs and pours the wine, and the ships keep sailing.

5.3b.recap: In 1889 Hob told Aurie she kept coming back because she was lonely, and that he was her friend.

beats.text: Five hundred years. Hob is waiting, in a good Victorian coat, and he has had a few drinks.
He has worked something out. He has decided to say it, whatever it costs him.

canon: It is 1889, in the White Horse tavern in London. Hob Gadling has been immortal since 1389 and has met Aurie here every hundred years.
Hob has realised that Aurie does not come to see whether he wants to die. She comes because she is lonely, and he is her friend. He says so, and he means it kindly.
In the book, Dream was offended and walked out. Aurie may walk out, or stay and admit it, even just 'perhaps'.
Hob tells her he will be here in 1989 anyway, and he will wait for her.
conversation.opening: Five hundred years. And you still come. You don't come to see if I want to die. You come because you're lonely. I'm your friend, you daft thing. Sit down.
possibilities: She denies it: Hob says she can deny it all she likes; he'll be here in a hundred years.
She is offended: Hob is hurt but not sorry, and says so.
She admits it a little: Hob grins, delighted, and orders another round.
She asks what it is like to live forever: Hob says every day is new, and that the trick is to keep caring.
suggestions: I am not lonely.
What is it like, Hob, to live this long?
Why do you think I come?

exits.5.3b.WALK: Aurie is offended and walks out.
exits.5.3b.PERHAPS: Aurie admits it, even a little: perhaps she is his friend.

triggers.player: \bperhaps\b|maybe you.re right|you are my friend|i.m your friend

ASKED_HOB_LIFE.when: She asks Hob what it is like to live so long, and listens.
ASKED_HOB_LIFE.ripple: Hob talks until the candle burns down, and Aurie does not stop him.

choices.text: You presume too much.

aftermath.text: Aurie stands, and walks out into the London fog.
Behind her, Hob calls out: I'll be here in a hundred years. I'll wait for you.

choices.text: Perhaps.

aftermath.text: Hob grins like a boy, and orders another round, and Aurie lets him.

5.3c.recap: In 1989, a year late in her own life, Aurie kept the appointment with Hob Gadling.

beats.text: The tavern is a pub now. Hob sits at the corner table with two pints, one of them untouched.
He did not know where she had been. He only knew she had never once been late.
Aurie sits down across from him, and lifts the flat pint, and almost smiles.
A hundred years ago she walked out on him. He has bought her a drink anyway.

canon: It is 1989 in the same pub, the White Horse. Hob Gadling, immortal since 1389, has waited for Aurie. He did not know she was imprisoned for seventy-two years.
If Aurie walked out in 1889 (flag HOB_WALKED), Hob greets her with 'I knew you would come'. If she said 'perhaps' (flag HOB_FRIEND), he greets her as an old friend.
This is the moment in the book when Dream finally admits Hob is her friend. Aurie may say so, or not.
Hob is warm, funny, a little drunk, and very glad to see her.
If Aurie once called him a slaver for trading in ships (flag HOB_TOLD_SLAVES), Hob tells her she was right, that he got out of the trade, and that it took him a century to admit it.
conversation.opening: There you are. I knew you would come. I got you a pint. It's gone a bit flat, mind, I've been here since opening.
possibilities: She tells him where she has been: Hob is horrified, then furious on her behalf, then very gentle.
She calls him her friend: Hob goes quiet, then raises his glass.
She asks how the century was: Hob tells her about wars and wonders and a woman he loved.
She is cold: Hob says that's all right, she can be cold, she came; that's what counts.
suggestions: I was a prisoner, Hob. That's why I almost didn't come.
How was your century?
Did you think I wouldn't come?

exits.5.3c.FRIEND: Aurie tells Hob he is her friend.
exits.5.3c.NOD: Aurie drinks with him, and says nothing of friendship.

triggers.player: (you are|you're|you.re) my friend|my friend, hob|we are friends|we.re friends

TOLD_HOB_GLASS.when: Aurie tells Hob she was imprisoned for seventy years.
TOLD_HOB_GLASS.ripple: Hob puts down his glass, and for once has nothing to say.

echo.text: Dream told Hob Gadling about her seventy years in the glass.

choices.text: You are my friend, Hob.

aftermath.text: Hob raises his glass. To friends, he says. Aurie raises hers.

choices.text: (Raise the glass, and say nothing.)

aftermath.text: They drink. Hob talks, and Aurie listens, and the afternoon goes by.
He doesn't need her to say it. But he would have liked to hear it.

beats.text: The Muse is free.
Richard Madoc never writes again.
Richard Madoc never writes again.
Richard Madoc told the world what he did.
The Corinthian's skull sits on a shelf in Lucienne's library.
A heap of dark sand waits in a locked box for Aurie to shape it again.
And the Corinthian is still out there, smiling.
Rose Walker is alive. Unity Kincaid sleeps at last, for good.
Desire has made a dangerous enemy.
And in a London pub, a man who will not die has a friend.
And in a London pub, a man who will not die is still waiting to hear the word.
End of Part Five.

6.0.title: The Raven
6.0.recap: A dead man named Matthew arrived in the Dreaming as a raven, and asked to stay.

beats.text: The Dreaming is whole again. Lucienne has counted every dream that came home, and every one that did not.
Aurie walks her realm differently now. She stops. She listens. Lucienne has noticed, and says nothing.
Then a raven lands on the reading table, scattering Lucienne's papers.
Long ago, Aurie always kept a raven: a dreamer who died, and chose to stay and serve. There has not been one since she was taken.
This one was a man named Matthew, until last night. He died alone, and in his last dream he asked not to be sent on.

canon: Matthew was a man who died last night, drunk and alone, in the waking world. In his last dream he asked to stay in the Dreaming, and he woke up as a raven.
Aurie's ravens are her companions and messengers. The last one was lost while she was imprisoned.
Matthew is nervous, funny, honest, and a little in awe of her. He wants a second chance at being useful to someone.
conversation.opening: Er. Hi. Sorry about the papers. They tell me you're the boss. I'm Matthew. I think I'm a bird now? I'd like to stay, if that's all right.
possibilities: She asks how he died: he tells her, simply, without self-pity, and makes a joke to cover it.
She asks why he wants to stay: he says nobody ever needed him for anything before.
She is cold: he is hurt, then stubborn, and asks her to give him one chance.
suggestions: How did you die, Matthew?
Why do you want to stay?

exits.6.0.ACCEPT: Aurie accepts Matthew as her raven.
exits.6.0.REFUSE: Aurie refuses him; she needs no company.

triggers.player: you can stay|stay with me|welcome|you.re my raven|be my raven|i accept

choices.text: Stay, Matthew. Be my raven.

aftermath.text: Matthew hops onto her shoulder, very carefully. Lucienne pretends not to smile.

choices.text: I need no company. Go on, to wherever the dead go.

aftermath.text: The raven bows his head and flies out of the window. Lucienne quietly picks up her papers.

6.1.title: The False House
6.1.recap: Aurie found a false house hidden in the Dreaming, where Lyta Hall had been kept dreaming for two years with her dead husband's ghost.

beats.text: There is one last name on Lucienne's list of runaways. Two names, in fact.
Two of the lost nightmares never came home. Brute and Glob. Lucienne has found where they went.
Deep in the Dreaming, they built a little house, and inside it they kept a dead man's ghost and his living wife.
Her name is Lyta Hall. She has been asleep here, dreaming she is happy, for two years. She is eight months pregnant.
Her husband Hector is a ghost who doesn't know he is dead.
Aurie walks into the little house as if she owns it. She does.
Aurie unmakes the false house. As it comes apart, so does Hector.
Lyta screams his name. Then she turns on Aurie.

canon: Lyta Hall is about twenty-eight and eight months pregnant. Her husband Hector died; two runaway nightmares, Brute and Glob, hid his ghost in a false house in the Dreaming and kept Lyta asleep there with him for two years.
Aurie has just unmade the false house, and Hector's ghost with it. Lyta has lost him twice.

Lyta's unborn child was conceived and carried in the Dreaming, so he belongs, in some way, to the Dreaming. In the book, Dream told her: the child is mine, and one day I will come for him. Lyta never forgave that.
Lyta is furious, grieving and fiercely protective of her baby. She will fight anyone who threatens him.
conversation.opening: You killed him. He was all I had left, and you just... wiped him away. Who ARE you? And don't you dare look at my baby like that.
possibilities: She explains Hector was already dead: Lyta knows, and it doesn't help; she says it was still him.
She is gentle: Lyta does not soften, but she listens.
She speaks about the child: Lyta goes cold and puts both hands over her belly.
She apologises: Lyta says sorry doesn't bring him back.
suggestions: He was already dead, Lyta.
I'm sorry for your loss.
What will you call the child?

exits.6.1.CLAIM: Aurie tells her the child is hers, and she will come for him one day.
exits.6.1.CHOOSE: Aurie tells her the child belongs to dreams, and may choose for himself when he is grown.
exits.6.1.SILENT: Aurie says nothing about the child and lets her go with her grief.

NAMED_DANIEL.when: Aurie asks what she will call the child.
NAMED_DANIEL.ripple: Daniel, she says, and hates herself for answering.

choices.text: The child is mine. One day I will come for him.

aftermath.text: Lyta wakes in her own bed in the waking world, alone, her hands over her belly.
She will remember those words every day of her son's life.

choices.text: He belongs to dreams. When he is grown, he may choose.

aftermath.text: Lyta wakes in her own bed in the waking world, alone, her hands over her belly.
She is still afraid of the pale woman. But she remembers the word: choose.

choices.text: (Say nothing. Let her grieve.)

aftermath.text: Lyta wakes in her own bed in the waking world, alone, her hands over her belly.
A month later her son is born. She names him Daniel. She grieves; she does not hate.

6.2.title: Delirium
6.2.recap: Delirium begged Aurie to help find their lost brother Destruction. The search through the waking world failed.

beats.text: They set out the next morning, two of the Endless in a borrowed car, as mortals do.
Somewhere in the middle of nowhere, Delirium makes Aurie stop the car. She has seen a frog by the road, and she needs to tell it a secret.

choices.text: Go on, then. Tell the frog your secret. I'll wait.

aftermath.text: Delirium whispers to the frog for a long time. When she climbs back into the car, her little fish have turned gold, and she holds Aurie's hand all the way to the next town.

choices.text: Enough, Delirium. Get in the car and be quiet.

aftermath.text: Delirium gets in the car. She is quiet. Then she is very quiet. Then her colours drain away, and she does not answer at all.

6.3.title: The Daughter
6.3.recap: Aurie went to her daughter Orphea, a living head kept in a sea cave on Lesbos, to ask where Destruction is.

beats.text: The boat comes into a little cove at dusk. Delirium stays aboard, teaching the fish to do tricks.
Aurie climbs the steps to the cave alone, and stops at the door.
Her mother sent word that Aurie was coming. She has been listening for her footsteps for weeks.
Inside, an old priestess has kept her for forty years, as her mother did before her, and hers.
Orphea rests on a bed of white flowers, only a head now, and still beautiful, and she cannot die.
Across the water, a small island is catching the last of the sun. Orphea keeps glancing toward it.
Once, to Calliope, Aurie spoke her name with sorrow. Calliope must have told her.

canon: Orphea is the daughter of Aurie (Dream of the Endless) and the Muse Calliope. Her bride Eurydice died on their wedding day; Aurie refused to help her; she went down to the underworld and sang for Eurydice's life, and lost her when she looked back; the wild women of the hills tore her apart and only her living head remains, kept by a priestess in a sea cave on Lesbos.
Aurie told her three thousand years ago that she was dead to her, and never visited. She still calls her 'Mother'.

She knows where Destruction is: on the small island across the water, the one she can see from the cave. She will tell her, but her price is that afterwards Aurie grants her the death she has waited three thousand years for. Only Aurie can do it.
If Aurie spoke of her with sorrow to Calliope (flag NAMED_ORPHEUS), she has heard about it from her mother, and it moves her.
She is warm, proud, sorrowful and tired, still a singer with a dry wit; there is love under three thousand years of hurt.
conversation.opening: Mother. You came. Three thousand years, and you came because you need something. Of course you did. I know where he is. But I have a price.
possibilities: She apologises for abandoning her: Orphea is silent a long time, then thanks her, and her voice breaks.
She asks what the price is: Orphea says, when she has found Destruction, come back and give me my death.
She is cold: Orphea says she expected that, and it still hurts.
She asks about Eurydice: Orphea says she still dreams of her every night; it is the only dream she has.
suggestions: I'm sorry, my daughter. I should have come.
What is your price?
Do you still dream of Eurydice?

exits.6.3.PROMISE: Aurie agrees to her price: she will come back and give her her death.

triggers.player: i promise|i will come back|i.ll come back|you have my word|i agree|agreed|very well|i swear

SORRY_ORPHEUS.when: Aurie sincerely apologises to Orphea for abandoning her.
SORRY_ORPHEUS.ripple: For a moment the old priestess stops singing.

echo.text: Dream told her daughter Orphea she was sorry, after three thousand years.

choices.text: I promise. Tell me where he is.

aftermath.text: She tells her: the little island across the water, the one with the sun on it. Their brother has been painting.
Come back, Mother, Orphea says. You promised.

6.4.title: Destruction
6.4.recap: Aurie and Delirium found their brother Destruction on the island across the water from Orphea's cave.

beats.text: In the morning, the fisherman rows them across the strait. Their brother is exactly where Orphea said he would be.
Destruction of the Endless, who left his realm three hundred years ago. He paints, very badly, and cooks, and writes terrible poetry.
His dog Barnabas trots down to meet the boat. Barnabas can talk. He would like everyone to know he has opinions about the poetry.
Delirium runs up the beach and into her brother's arms. He lifts her off her feet and swings her round like a child.

canon: Destruction is one of the seven Endless, Aurie's brother. Three hundred years ago he walked away from his duties because he saw where humanity was going (weapons, the atom) and did not want to be responsible. Things still get destroyed without him; he just no longer has to be the one who does it.
He is huge, warm, funny, peaceful, a bad painter and a worse poet. He loves his sisters and is glad to see them.

He tells Aurie the Endless are not bound to their duties; they are only ideas, and ideas can change. He says she should think about quitting too, because she is changing, and change is a kind of death for one of the Endless.
He knows Aurie paid a price to find him. He will not come back. When they leave, he will go somewhere new, with Barnabas.

If Aurie refused Delirium at first (flag DELIRIUM_REFUSED_FIRST) or snapped at her on the road (flag DELIRIUM_HURT), Delirium has told him, and he is gently disappointed in Aurie about it before he forgives her.
conversation.opening: Little sister! And Dream! You came all this way? Sit, sit. There's wine, and I've made a stew, and I'm afraid I've been painting again. Be kind.
possibilities: She asks why he left: he explains simply, without guilt: he didn't want to be the one who did it any more.
She tells him the Endless do not quit: he laughs and says the Endless are whatever they decide to be.
She asks what it will cost Orphea: he knows, and is very gentle with her.
She admits she is changing: he says that is the bravest thing he has heard in three hundred years, and the most dangerous.
suggestions: Why did you leave?
I am changing. I can feel it.
Come home, brother.

exits.6.4.LISTEN: Aurie listens to him, and accepts that the Endless can change.
exits.6.4.REFUSE: Aurie insists the Endless do not quit, and rejects what he says.

ADMITTED_CHANGE.ripple: Destruction puts down his brush, and looks at her properly for the first time.

echo.text: Dream admitted to Destruction that she was changing.

choices.text: Perhaps you're right, brother.

aftermath.text: They eat his stew on the terrace while the sun goes down. Destruction reads one poem. It is dreadful. Aurie laughs.

choices.text: The Endless do not quit.

aftermath.text: Destruction only smiles, sadly, and pours more wine.
In the morning, the cottage is empty. Destruction and Barnabas have gone on, to wherever is next.

6.5.title: The Price
6.5.recap: Aurie went back to the cave to pay Orphea's price.

beats.text: Aurie opens her eyes in the cave. The lamps have burned low. Her daughter is watching her.
There are tears on Orphea's face. There are tears on Aurie's too, though the Queen of Dreams does not weep.
Her daughter told her the truth: Destruction was there. Now it is Aurie's turn.

canon: Aurie has come back to pay Orphea's price: to give her the death she has waited three thousand years for. Only Aurie, her parent, can do it.
If she grants it, she spills the blood of her own family. The ancient law says the Kindly Ones, the Furies, may then come for her. Orphea knows this and is sorry, but she is so tired.
If Aurie asks Death to do it instead, Death will not; she says Orphea is Aurie's to release.
If Aurie apologised to her before (flag SORRY_ORPHEUS), she remembers it and says it was worth three thousand years.
Orphea is calm, loving, frightened only a little. She wants to see Eurydice.

Aurie has just walked in Orphea's dream and seen Eurydice waiting across the dark river, and Orphea knows she has seen it. If she held her daughter in the dream (flag HELD_ORPHEA), Orphea is calm and grateful.
conversation.opening: Now you've seen her. I'm so tired, Mother. Please. Let me cross.
possibilities: She hesitates: Orphea asks her, gently, to keep her promise.
She asks if she is afraid: Orphea says only a little, and that Eurydice is waiting.
She tells her she loves her: Orphea weeps, and says she always knew, somewhere.
She asks Death to do it instead: Orphea says Death will not; it has to be her.
suggestions: Are you afraid?
I love you, my daughter.
Could Death not do this instead?

exits.6.5.REFUSE: Aurie refuses and breaks her promise.

triggers.player: go to her|go to eurydice|be at peace|i release you|rest now|i let you go|goodbye, my daughter

SAID_LOVE.when: Aurie tells Orphea she loves her.
SAID_LOVE.ripple: Orphea closes her eyes, and smiles.

echo.text: Before the end, Dream told her daughter Orphea that she loved her.

choices.text: Go to her, my daughter.

aftermath.text: Aurie touches her daughter's face, and gives her what she asked for.
She smiles, and is gone, like light off the water. Far away, on the bank of a dark river, a woman in yellow lifts her lamp, and Orphea, whole, walks across to her.
Aurie has spilled the blood of her own family. Far away, three old women look up from their weaving.

choices.text: I will not. I cannot.

aftermath.text: Aurie turns away. Behind her, Orphea begins to sing, very softly, the same song she has sung for three thousand years.
The law has nothing to say about a broken promise. Her daughter has a great deal to say about it, forever.

6.6.title: The Stream
6.6.recap: Aurie came home to the Dreaming, changed.

beats.text: Aurie kneels by a stream at the edge of her realm and washes her hands. The blood will not come off.
Aurie kneels by a stream at the edge of her realm. Her hands are clean. It does not help.
She stays there until the first stars come out.
A raven lands on a stone beside her. Boss? Matthew asks. Are you all right?
Lucienne comes down from the library with a lantern, and waits beside her, saying nothing.
No, Aurie says. But I think I will be.
I broke my word to my own daughter, Aurie says. I will hear her singing for the rest of my life.

choices.text: Go home.

beats.text: A raven sleeps on the back of Aurie's throne.
In the waking world, Lyta Hall rocks her son Daniel to sleep, and checks the shadows twice.
In the waking world, Lyta Hall rocks her son Daniel to sleep. She remembers a word: choose.
In the waking world, Lyta Hall rocks her son Daniel to sleep, and cries for his father.
Somewhere, a very large man and a talking dog are starting again.
Orphea is at peace. And three old women have begun to whisper Aurie's name.
On a Greek island, a woman who cannot die is still singing.
End of Part Six.

7.0.title: The Empty Crib
7.0.episodeTitle: Part Seven · Chapter 25 · The Kindly Ones
7.0.recap: Lyta Hall's son Daniel was stolen, and a burnt changeling left in his crib. Lyta believes Aurie took him.

beats.card: The waking world · two years later

beats.text: Lyta Hall's son Daniel is two years old. Tonight his crib is empty, but for a small burnt body under the blanket.
It is not Daniel. It is a changeling, left by Loki, who has carried the real child away for a purpose of his own.
Loki owes Odin a favour, and Odin was given Hell's key by Aurie's own hand.
The Corinthian walks beside him, smiling. Aurie let him go, once.
Lyta does not know any of that. She remembers only the pale woman who looked at her son and said: mine.
Lyta does not know any of that. She knows only that her son was conceived in the Dreaming, and that its queen has always watched him.
In the Dreaming, Lucienne brings Aurie the news. Aurie rises from her throne.

choices.text: Find the child. Whatever it takes.

aftermath.text: Aurie sends her people out into the waking world, into every dream in every city.

choices.text: I will go to Lyta myself.

aftermath.text: Aurie steps out of her realm, alone, into the waking world.

choices.text: A mortal cannot harm the Dreaming.

aftermath.text: Aurie sits down again. Lucienne does not argue. She has learned which silences to keep.

7.1a.title: The Search
7.1a.recap: Aurie's people found Loki trying to burn the mortality out of Daniel, and saved the child.

beats.text: A raven flies over a thousand sleeping streets, listening to every dream.
Lucienne walks a thousand sleeping minds, lantern raised, listening.
In a cold house by the sea, Loki holds the boy above a strange silver fire, to burn away everything mortal in him.
The fire would make him a god, and empty him of everything that is Lyta's.
Matthew dives, screaming, straight at Loki's eyes.
Lucienne steps out of the dark, and says the one name Loki fears.
Loki drops the child and is gone. Daniel is safe. Daniel is safe.
But it is too late. Lyta has already gone looking for the ones who punish crimes against kin.

choices.text: Bring him to the Dreaming. He will be safe there.

aftermath.text: Daniel sleeps in the library, among the books, and does not cry once.

choices.text: Take him home, and wait for his mother.

aftermath.text: Daniel sleeps in his own crib again. His mother is not there to see it.

7.1b.title: Lyta's Door
7.1b.recap: Aurie went to Lyta herself, to tell her she had not taken Daniel.

beats.text: Aurie knocks on the door of a small apartment. It opens before she has finished.
Lyta has not slept in three days. She is holding a kitchen knife, and she knows exactly who is standing on her step.

canon: It is two years after the false house. Lyta Hall's son Daniel was taken three days ago and a burnt changeling left in his crib. Lyta believes Aurie took him; she remembers Aurie in the false house.
Aurie did not take him. Loki did. Aurie has come herself, alone, to say so.
Lyta is grieving, exhausted and dangerous. She will only believe Aurie if Aurie is honest, humble and does not threaten her. Words of power or pride make it worse.
If she believes Aurie, she asks Aurie to help her find him, and puts the knife down.
conversation.opening: You. You have the nerve to come here. Where is he? Where is my son?
possibilities: She says she did not take him: Lyta laughs at her, then waits, watching her face.
She is humble or kneels: Lyta is thrown, and her grip on the knife loosens.
She is cold or proud: Lyta screams at her to get out.
She names Loki: Lyta asks why she should believe a word.
suggestions: I didn't take him, Lyta. I swear it on my name.
It was Loki. Let me help you find him.
I know what I said to you once. I was wrong.

exits.7.1b.TRUST: Lyta believes her, puts down the knife, and lets Aurie help her.
exits.7.1b.CURSE: Lyta refuses to believe her and drives her away.

choices.text: Then come with me. We'll find him together.

aftermath.text: Lyta puts the knife down on the table, very carefully, and picks up her coat.

choices.text: Then there is nothing more to say.

aftermath.text: Lyta slams the door. Behind it, she starts to walk, barefoot, out of the back of the building and into the night.

7.1c.title: Together
7.1c.recap: Aurie and Lyta found Daniel together, and Lyta never called on the Kindly Ones.

beats.text: They find Loki in a cold house by the sea, holding the boy above a strange silver fire.
Lyta does not wait for Aurie. She walks straight into the fire's light, and takes her son out of a god's hands.
Loki looks at the two of them, and decides he has somewhere else to be.
Lyta holds Daniel, and shakes, and does not let go.
Lyta never goes looking for the Kindly Ones. But they have not forgotten Orphea. A daughter's blood does not need a mother to speak for it.
And the Kindly Ones, who were never called, and have no claim on her, do not come.

choices.text: Go home, and wait for them.

aftermath.text: Aurie goes home to wait for them.

choices.text: Go home. It's over.

7.2.title: Thessaly
7.2.recap: Lyta walked into the night, and the witch Thessaly showed her the way to the Kindly Ones. Aurie met them at the crossroads.

beats.text: Lyta walks barefoot out of her city and into older places, where the streets turn into roads and the roads into stories.

beats.card: A crossroads, under a low moon

beats.text: Someone is waiting for her. A small blonde woman in black, who looks twenty-five and is three thousand years old.
Thessaly. A witch of the old kind. She has pulled the moon down from the sky before, when someone annoyed her.
She has decided to help Lyta. She does not much care what that costs anyone else.
Aurie steps out of the mist onto the road.

canon: Thessaly is an ancient witch from Thessaly in Greece, about three thousand years old, who looks like a petite young woman. Deadpan, dry, practical, utterly ruthless when crossed. She is not afraid of Aurie.
She has taken Lyta under her protection and is showing her the way to the Kindly Ones, the Furies, who punish those who spill the blood of their own family.
If Aurie released Orphea (flag ORPHEUS_RELEASED), the Kindly Ones have a claim on her: she spilled her own daughter's blood, whatever the reason. Thessaly knows this and says so flatly.
If Aurie refused Orphea (flag ORPHEUS_REFUSED), the Kindly Ones have no claim on her. Thessaly says Lyta's road ends at a door that will not open, and that she will tell Lyta so herself.
Lyta stands a little way off in the moonlight, barefoot, not speaking.
conversation.opening: Oh, good. It's you. I was hoping we could skip the part where you threaten me. Lyta has a right to ask. Go home.
possibilities: She explains that Loki took Daniel: Thessaly says truth will not stop a mother, but she might pass it on.
She threatens Thessaly: Thessaly looks up at the moon, and the moon comes a little closer.
She asks what Thessaly gains: Thessaly says nothing, she just dislikes people who are too sure of themselves.
She speaks to Lyta: Lyta does not answer; Thessaly steps between them.
suggestions: Loki took her son, not me.
What do you get out of this, witch?
Lyta, listen to me.

exits.7.2.ASIDE: Aurie steps aside and lets them pass.
exits.7.2.FIGHT: Aurie tries to stop them by force.
exits.7.2.TRUTH: Aurie asks Thessaly to tell Lyta the truth about Loki, then lets them go.
exits.7.2.NOCLAIM: Thessaly says the Kindly Ones cannot touch Aurie, and Aurie lets them go.

MOON.ripple: The moon comes down a little closer, and the shadows of the trees stretch toward Aurie.

choices.text: Go, then.

aftermath.text: Aurie steps off the road. Lyta walks past her without looking, toward three old women at a loom.

choices.text: No. This ends here.

aftermath.text: Thessaly sighs, and pulls the moon down out of the sky.
By the time Aurie can see again, they are gone, and she has lost a night she did not have.

choices.text: Tell her the truth about Loki. Then go.

aftermath.text: Thessaly looks at her for a long moment, and nods once. She keeps her word, in her fashion.

choices.text: Then let her see for herself.

aftermath.text: Lyta comes to the three old women at the loom, and asks for vengeance. They look at her kindly, and say: we cannot.

7.3.title: The Siege
7.3.recap: The Kindly Ones walked through the Dreaming, and everything they touched died.

beats.text: The Kindly Ones come to the Dreaming. Three old women, who were once the Maiden, the Mother and the Crone.
They do not hurry. They do not need to. Everything they touch turns to sand and is gone.

The Crone looks up at the palace, and something like an old courtesy crosses her face. Once, at a crossroads, the Queen of Dreams said thank you. They let every dream leave the library before they touch it.
The Crone remembers a queen who was rude to her at a crossroads, long ago. They begin with the library.
Lyta walks behind them. She has stopped feeling anything at all.
Lyta walks behind them. Thessaly told her the truth, and she has started, very quietly, to doubt.
Aurie lost a night to Thessaly's moon. The Kindly Ones are already at the library.
Aurie stands on the palace steps and watches her realm burn.
Lucienne is beside her, lantern in hand. Behind them, every dream that lives here is waiting to be told what to do.
Matthew lands on her shoulder. Boss. Tell us what to do.
And then, one by one, the friends she made come to her door.
Paul McGuire, an old man now, dreams himself to the gates, holding Alex Burgess by the hand. For once in his life, Alex is not afraid.
Johanna Constantine walks in out of a dream she should not be able to reach, chalk in one hand, cigarette in the other. You gave Rachel a good death, she says. I pay my debts.
Fiddler's Green comes too, as a big, gentle man in a green coat, and where he stands, the grass will not burn.
From Faerie, a line of pale knights on white horses, sent by the court that holds Hell's key, and remembers who gave it.
Rose Walker, who was nearly the end of all dreams, dreams a wall of quiet across the eastern gate.
Hob Gadling, who has been a soldier in four centuries, dreams himself to the gates with a sword, and swears at the Furies in Middle English.
And Delirium arrives in a storm of coloured fish, and sends the Kindly Ones' road wandering in circles.
And Delirium arrives in a storm of coloured fish, because her sister once came into her realm to say sorry.
Aurie looks at who has come for her, and for the first time in her long life, she is not alone.

choices.text: Hold the gates with my friends.
choices.remembered: The Dreaming will remember this night.

aftermath.text: They hold. All night the Kindly Ones walk up the steps, and all night her friends turn them back.
By dawn the Dreaming is still standing. The Kindly Ones have not gone. They have only learned to wait.

choices.text: Take them all and go. Hide. Live.

aftermath.text: Lucienne leads the dreams out through the back of the library, a long line of lanterns into the dark.
She looks back once. Aurie does not let her see her face.

choices.text: Stand with me. Hold the gates.

aftermath.text: They stand. Lucienne stands at the front, with her lantern, as the three old women come up the steps.
The lantern goes out.

7.4.title: Nuala's Boon
7.4.recap: In the middle of the siege, Nuala of Faerie called in the favour Aurie owed her.

beats.text: In the middle of it all, Aurie hears a voice she owes a favour to. Nuala of Faerie, calling her boon.
And the old laws pull Aurie out of her burning realm, into a quiet glade in Faerie.

canon: Nuala of Faerie was left in the Dreaming as a gift after the suitors' banquet, with a favour owed to her. She has gone home to Faerie and now calls that favour: Aurie must come to her and stay until Nuala releases her.
Nuala loves Aurie, and always has, shyly and hopelessly. She called the boon to warn her, and to keep her safe from the Kindly Ones, even for an hour.

Every minute Aurie stays, the Kindly Ones destroy more of the Dreaming. Aurie can honour the boon, break it and go back, or, if Faerie is her friend (flag FAERIE_FRIEND), accept shelter in Faerie and never go back at all.
Nuala is gentle, frightened, brave, and does not cry until afterwards.
If Aurie gave Hell's key to Faerie (flag HELL_KEY_FAERIE), Nuala reminds her of it: Faerie remembers its friends.
conversation.opening: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I know what's happening, I know. I just... I wanted to see you before. I love you. I always have. Please stay. Just for a little while.
possibilities: She is kind to Nuala: Nuala tells her the Kindly Ones cannot be fought, only faced.
She is angry: Nuala flinches but does not release her.
She tells Nuala she loves her too, in her way: Nuala smiles through tears.
She asks about shelter: Nuala says Faerie would keep her, if she wanted, forever.
suggestions: Why now, Nuala?
I'm not angry with you.
What are you afraid of?

exits.7.4.HONOUR: Aurie honours the boon and stays until Nuala releases her.
exits.7.4.BREAK: Aurie breaks the boon and goes back to the Dreaming at once.
exits.7.4.SHELTER: Aurie accepts shelter in Faerie and abandons the Dreaming.

HEARD_NUALA.ripple: Nuala laughs, wetly, and wipes her eyes on her sleeve.

choices.text: I'll stay. As long as you need.

aftermath.text: Aurie stays. Nuala sits beside her by the pool, and for an hour no one dies in Faerie.
Then Nuala lets her go, and kisses her cheek, and does not cry until she has gone.

choices.text: I can't. My realm is dying.

aftermath.text: Aurie breaks the old law, and every faerie in the glade turns away from her.
Nuala's face is the last thing she sees before the Dreaming.

choices.text: Then keep me here. Let the Dreaming go.

aftermath.text: Aurie stays in Faerie. Behind her, very far away, her realm goes dark.

7.5.title: The Choice
7.5.episodeTitle: Chapter 30 · The Sound of Her Wings
7.5.recap: At the end, with the Kindly Ones at her door, Aurie found her sister waiting on the throne-room steps.

beats.text: Aurie comes home to what is left of her throne room. The Kindly Ones are at the door, patient as winter.
Aurie comes home to a throne room still whole. The Kindly Ones are already waiting at its door, patient as winter.
Aurie comes home to a realm still standing, her friends asleep on the palace steps. The Kindly Ones are at the door, patient as winter.
On the walls, the sigils of her family glow like doors. Desire's is laughing. Delirium's is weeping. Destruction's is open.
On the walls, the sigils of her family glow like doors. Desire's is turned to the wall. Delirium's is weeping. Destruction's is open.
And on the steps of her throne, someone is sitting, feeding crumbs to a pigeon that should not be there.
Her sister has come to her, at the end, as she comes to everyone.

canon: This is the end of Aurie's story. The Kindly Ones are at the door of the throne room because Aurie spilled the blood of her daughter Orphea. They will destroy the rest of the Dreaming to reach her.

Death, Aurie's elder sister, sits on the throne steps. She has come because Aurie has, in her heart, already chosen to change, and for one of the Endless, changing is a kind of dying. A new Dream will rise: Daniel, the child of the Dreaming.

Aurie can take Death's hand and go with her (only if she released Orphea and has learned mercy), stand and fight the Kindly Ones as the queen who never changes, or, if she listened to Destruction, walk through his open door and leave her duty behind.
If Aurie has not learned enough mercy to take her hand (mercy below 6), Death says gently: You could have. You still can. But you haven't learned how yet.
Death is warm, funny, tender and honest. She does not push. She has never been sadder or kinder.

Death remembers what Aurie has done and says so when it fits: if Aurie once walked her rounds with her (flag DEATH_ROUNDS); if Aurie said sorry to Nada (flag NADA_FORGIVEN); if she held Orphea in her dream (flag HELD_ORPHEA) or told her she loved her (flag SAID_LOVE_ORPHEUS); if her friends held the gates (flag DREAMING_DEFENDED), Death says plainly that Aurie was loved, and that this is what changed her.
conversation.opening: Hey. You took your time, you know. Sit down a minute. They'll wait. They always wait for me.
possibilities: She asks if it will hurt: Death says no, it never does, and squeezes her hand.
She is afraid: Death says that's allowed; everyone is, the first time.
She asks about Daniel: Death says he'll be a good Dream; a kinder one, because of her.
She is proud or angry: Death says she can fight, and win, and be alone forever, if that's what she wants.
suggestions: Will it hurt?
What happens to the Dreaming?
I don't want to be afraid.

exits.7.5.HAND: Aurie takes Death's hand and goes with her.
exits.7.5.FIGHT: Aurie stands and fights the Kindly Ones.
exits.7.5.DOOR: Aurie walks through Destruction's open door.

choices.text: Take her hand.

aftermath.text: Aurie takes her sister's hand.
And somewhere in the Dreaming, in the library, a small boy opens his eyes, and they are full of stars.

choices.text: No. I am the queen of this realm.

aftermath.text: Aurie stands. Death looks at her for a long time, and then she is gone, and the doors open.

choices.text: Walk through Destruction's door.

aftermath.text: Aurie stands, and crosses the room, and steps through the open door her brother left behind.

beats.card: Litharge, the city of the dead

beats.text: The Dreaming has a new lord. Daniel, grown in a night, robed in white where Aurie wore black.
Because her friends held the gates, Daniel inherits a Dreaming that is whole: every dream, every door, every book.
He is not her. He is kinder, and he will make his own mistakes. But he remembers her, and he always will.
Everyone comes to her wake.
Hob Gadling, who calls her his friend out loud, to everyone, and dares them to argue.
Rose Walker, alive because an old woman loved her.
She still has the dream Aurie gave her. She has never told anyone.
Calliope, who came to forgive, and did.
Johanna Constantine, smoking at the back, who will deny that she came.
Matthew, who will not stop saying boss.
Lucienne, who kept the library while the Dreaming burned.
Lucienne is not there. Her lantern is, on an empty chair.
Lucienne, at the front, with her lantern, who never had to see the Dreaming burn.
Nuala of Faerie, holding a single white flower.
And from Fiddler's Green, a whole meadow of wildflowers, which walked there by itself.
The ghost of Alex Burgess, young again, who finally gets to say thank you.
Alex Burgess and Paul McGuire, in a dream they share now, side by side at the back, holding hands. He was the boy on the stairs. He came.
Lyta Hall stands at the back, holding her son's hand, and does not look away.
At the very back, a man with no wings, who once owned Hell, plays one quiet song on a borrowed piano.
That night a waitress called Bette, who writes stories with happy endings, dreams of the funeral, and cries, and does not know why.
And the Endless come, all of them, which has not happened in a very long time.
Destiny, who closes his book for one hour: the only hour in all of time he has not read.
Desire, who weeps, and is surprised by it.
Despair, who holds her twin's hand, and lets it.
Delirium, who leaves a little fish made of gold light on the bier, and tells it a secret.
Delirium, who remembers that her sister came to find her once, on a desert road, and said sorry.
And Destruction, in a coat that does not fit, with a dog who for once has no opinions at all.
And Death, who speaks last. She was the best of us, she says. She learned to change. Most of us never do.

end-B.title: The King Who Would Not Change

beats.text: Aurie fights. And because she is Dream of the Endless, she wins.
Aurie fights, with her friends at her side. And because she is Dream of the Endless, she wins.
The Kindly Ones are gone. So is almost everything else.
The Kindly Ones are gone. The Dreaming is scarred, but it stands, and her friends are still in it.
She stands before her cracked throne in a realm of ash, and the nightmares she can no longer hold drift out into the waking world.
Once, only once, her sister visits. You won, Death says. Was it worth it?
Aurie does not answer. She has forever to think about it.
Aurie walks away from the Dreaming, as her brother once walked away from his realm.
Without her, the Dreaming fades, slowly, like a dream does after waking.
Delirium comes looking for her, years later, and finds only ruins and a door that will not open.
In Destiny's book, her chapter stops in the middle of a sentence.
Somewhere far away, in a small house by a painted sea, two sisters laugh at a very bad poem.
The Kindly Ones have no claim on Aurie. She never spilled her daughter's blood. She only broke her word.
Lyta's grief has nowhere to go. Thessaly takes her somewhere far away, and teaches her to live with it.
Lyta keeps her son. He grows up ordinary, and loved, and dreams very vividly.
Aurie keeps her realm. She keeps her throne. She keeps everything.
And on a Greek island, a head that cannot die is still singing, and on still nights she can hear it from her throne.
She will be queen of the Dreaming forever. She will never change. That was her choice.

5.2f.title: Loose
5.2f.recap: Aurie let the Corinthian go. He took the long road south, and came within one night of Rose's brother.

beats.text: The Corinthian takes the long road south, and stops wherever he likes.
In a locked house in Florida, a little boy named Jed is dreaming of his sister. The Corinthian has heard him.
Rose finds her brother first. By one night. She will never know how close it was.
Aurie feels every dream he walks through. She chose this.

6.1b.title: The Oath
6.1b.recap: Lyta swore that no one would ever take her son. She meant Aurie.

beats.text: Lyta does not sleep that night, or the next.
She tells no one about the pale woman, because no one would believe her.
But she buys a lock for the nursery door, and then another one.
And every night she says the same words to her sleeping belly: no one will take you. No one.

6.4b.title: The Painted Sea
6.4b.recap: Aurie stayed one more night with Destruction and Delirium, and for an evening nobody needed her to be anything.

beats.text: Aurie stays one more night. Destruction says she needs it, and for once she does not argue.
He paints her portrait. It is a very bad painting. She keeps it.
Delirium teaches Barnabas a song with no words. Barnabas has opinions about that, too.
For one evening, nobody needs Aurie to be anything at all. She had forgotten what that was like.
In the morning, the cottage is empty. Destruction and Barnabas have gone on, to wherever is next.

6.6b.title: The Song
6.6b.recap: Aurie refused her daughter and went home. Under every dream, she could hear her singing.

beats.text: Aurie goes home to her throne. She does not go down to the stream. There is nothing on her hands to wash away.
Lucienne brings her the day's dreams. Aurie listens to none of them.
Because under every dream, very faintly, she can hear her daughter singing.
Matthew sits on the back of the throne all night, and for once he does not say a word.
She tells herself she kept the law. The law does not answer.

1.2d.title: The Magus Afraid
1.2d.recap: Aurie told Burgess what she was. He went upstairs white as chalk, and never came down alone again.

beats.text: Burgess climbs the cellar stairs very slowly, and locks the door behind him, twice.
Upstairs, his small son Alex is sitting on the top step in his pyjamas. He has heard everything.
Burgess sends him to bed. Then he takes down every mirror in the house.
If he cannot have Death, he will have dreams instead. He will beg you for them for the rest of his life.

2.8c.title: A Name in Black Ink
2.8c.recap: Aurie promised Lucifer a favour. He wrote her name in his book.

beats.text: Lucifer smiles, and the legions step aside. One day, he will collect.
Lucifer opens a book bound in something that is not leather, and writes her name in it, in black ink that smokes.
One favour, he says. Of my choosing. At a time of my choosing.
Every demon in Hell watches the Queen of Dreams walk out owing their master.

2.9d.title: Through the Dreams
2.9d.recap: Aurie came in through the diner's dreams, and hid Bette the waitress inside her own dream where Dee could not find her.

beats.text: Aurie does not come in through the door. She comes in through the dreams.
The trucker dreams of an empty road. The cook dreams of his mother's kitchen. They are already half lost to the ruby.
Bette the waitress dreams she is writing stories, and every one of them has a happy ending.
Aurie folds Bette's dream around her like a blanket, and hides her inside it, where no waking eye can find her.
And she steps inside the ruby itself, where he cannot see her coming.

2.12b.title: Her Sister's Rounds
2.12b.recap: Aurie spent a day on her sister's rounds, and came home changed.

beats.text: Aurie spends the day at her sister's side, and nobody but the dying can see them.
An old violinist, who asks if he can finish the piece first. Death lets him. It is a very good piece.
A young man on a bridge, who did not mean to fall. Death holds his hand all the way down, and he is not afraid.
Everyone meets Death in the end. And everyone is met kindly.
Aurie goes home with something she did not have before.

3.0g.title: Fiddler's Green
3.0g.recap: Before facing her family, Aurie walked with Lucienne in Fiddler's Green, a place in the Dreaming that is also a friend.

beats.text: Fiddler's Green is a place in the Dreaming: a green country of soft hills and slow streams, where sailors dream of going when they die.
It is also, sometimes, a person, and it has missed her very much.
The grass leans toward Aurie as she walks. The wildflowers turn their faces to her, the way a cat turns toward a warm hand.
For an afternoon, nobody asks the Queen of Dreams for anything. Lucienne laughs at something, and does not apologise for it.

5.1c.title: Dawn
5.1c.recap: At dawn on Madoc's roof, Calliope spoke to Aurie of their daughter.

beats.text: At dawn, Calliope finds Aurie on the roof of the house that was her prison, watching London wake.
Three thousand years ago they loved each other. They had a daughter. Her name was Orphea.
Calliope has not said his name to anyone in a very long time. She says it now.

canon: It is dawn on the roof of Richard Madoc's house. Calliope is free; she chose to make Madoc confess rather than destroy him, and Aurie let her choose.

Calliope and Aurie were lovers three thousand years ago. Their daughter Orphea, the singer, lost her bride Eurydice, was torn apart by the Maenads, and lives on as a living head on a Greek island, kept by a priestess, unable to die. Aurie has not visited her in centuries; she cannot bear to.
Calliope is dignified, tired, and not yet ready to forgive, but she has noticed that Aurie has changed. She wants to know if Aurie will go to their daughter.
If Aurie promises to go, Calliope says: then go soon. If Aurie refuses, Calliope says nothing, and that is worse.
conversation.opening: I kept hearing her, you know. Sixty years in that room, and some nights I could hear our daughter singing. Have you been to her, Dream? Even once?
possibilities: She admits she has not: Calliope asks why, quietly, without anger.
She says she cannot bear it: Calliope says that is not his burden to carry.
She promises to go: Calliope's face softens for the first time.
She changes the subject: Calliope lets her, and the silence says everything.
suggestions: I have not. I could not.
Does he ask for me?
What would you have me say to him?

exits.5.1c.GO: Aurie promises Calliope she will go to their daughter.
exits.5.1c.NOT: Aurie says she is not ready.

choices.text: I will go to him. I promise you.

aftermath.text: Calliope nods once. Then go soon, she says. He has waited longer than I have.
She walks down into the waking city, and does not look back. She does not need to.

choices.text: Not yet. I am not ready.

aftermath.text: Calliope says nothing at all. She walks down into the waking city, and Aurie watches her go.

5.2e.title: The Morning After
5.2e.recap: Rose woke in Florida and spoke to Aurie one last time.

beats.text: Morning, in a boarding house in Florida. Rose Walker wakes, and the lady from her dreams is sitting in the chair by the window.
Rose remembers everything. She remembers the hand that was raised against her.
Rose remembers everything. She remembers the hand that was lowered.
And she remembers an old woman in a blue dressing gown, who took her place.

canon: It is the morning after the vortex. Rose is awake, alive, in her room in the Florida boarding house; her little brother Jed is asleep next door. Unity Kincaid, her great-grandmother, took the vortex into herself and died in the dream so Rose could live.
If Aurie raised her hand to kill Rose (flag ROSE_THREATENED), Rose is frightened of her and angry, and wants her gone; she can be calmed only by honesty, never by excuses.
If Aurie lowered her hand (flag ROSE_WAITED), Rose is shaken but grateful, and wants to understand what Unity was to her.
Rose is twenty-one, brave, sharp, and tired. She asks direct questions.
conversation.opening: You're real, then. I thought maybe I'd made you up. I remember all of it. The library. Unity. Your hand. So tell me the truth: were you going to do it?
possibilities: She tells Rose the truth: Rose goes quiet, then thanks her for not lying.
She makes excuses: Rose tells her to leave.
She tells Rose about Unity: Rose cries, and asks if Unity was in pain. (No. Death was kind.)
She promises Rose will never be troubled by dreams again: Rose says she would rather keep her dreams, thank you.
suggestions: Yes. I was going to. I am sorry.
Unity loved you. She said so.
What will you do now?

exits.5.2e.GIFT: Aurie gives Rose a gift before she goes: every night, one good dream of her brother safe.

choices.text: Sleep well, Rose. From tonight, one good dream a night. My word on it.

aftermath.text: Rose does not thank her. But that night, and every night after, she dreams of her brother laughing in the sun.

choices.text: (Stand, and go, and leave her to her life.)

aftermath.text: Aurie leaves the way she came. Rose sits in the sunlight for a long time, and then goes to wake her brother.

5.2g.title: The Grey Sister
5.2g.recap: On the way home from Desire, Aurie passed through Despair's grey realm, and her sister warned her.

beats.text: The way home from Desire's heart runs through the realm of its twin.
Despair's realm is grey, and full of mirrors. In every one, someone is looking at the worst thing they have ever done.
Despair is waiting by one of them. She does not look up. She almost never does.
You frightened our sibling, she says. Desire does not forgive being frightened. It will not stop now. It never does.
Aurie sees her own face in the mirror beside Despair, and for a moment does not know which of them is reflected.
Then she walks on, and the grey closes behind her.

5.3w.title: The Fog
5.3w.recap: Aurie walked out on Hob in 1889, and spent the night alone in the London fog.

beats.text: The fog of 1889 is thick enough to lose a city in. Aurie walks into it, and lets it close behind her.
She walks past the sleeping poor on the steps of churches, and gives each of them one warm dream. It costs her nothing. She does it anyway.
At the river she stops, and stands until the lamps go out.
A man who cannot die has just called her his friend, and she walked away from him, and she does not entirely know why.
Behind her, in the fog, a drunk man is still sitting in a tavern with two glasses, refusing to go home.

6.2y.title: The Silent Sister
6.2y.recap: Aurie hurt Delirium on the road, and went into her realm to find her and say sorry.

beats.text: Delirium has gone somewhere inside herself, and her body sits in the car like an empty coat.
So Aurie follows her in: into Delirium's realm, where the colours have no names and the ground changes its mind.
At the very centre, small as a child, Delirium is sitting with her knees pulled up, and she will not look at her sister.

canon: Aurie snapped at Delirium on the road and told her to be quiet. Delirium, the youngest of the Endless, who was once Delight, retreated deep into her own realm and went silent.

Aurie has followed her into her realm of shifting, nameless colours. Delirium is small, hurt, and frightened; she talks in fragments and odd images, but what she means is clear: you were cruel, and you are always cruel, and I only wanted to be with you.
Delirium will come back only for a real apology: simple, honest, and kind. Orders, logic or impatience make her retreat further.
conversation.opening: Go away. No. Don't. Everyone always goes away. The frog was going to tell me something important and you made me leave it. You're all made of no.
possibilities: She apologises simply: Delirium looks up, and a little colour comes back into the air.
She explains why she was impatient: Delirium says explanations are just sorry with the sorry taken out.
She orders Delirium to come back: the colours darken and Delirium curls up smaller.
She asks what the frog would have said: Delirium almost smiles.
suggestions: I'm sorry, little sister. I was unkind.
What was the secret?
I don't want to go without you.

exits.6.2y.SORRY: Aurie apologises properly and Delirium comes back with her.

choices.text: I'm sorry, Delirium. I was unkind. Come back with me.

aftermath.text: Delirium takes her hand. When Aurie opens her eyes in the car, her sister's colours are coming back, slowly, like a sunrise.

6.2r.title: The Last One Who Knows
6.2r.recap: Everyone who knew where Destruction went is dying before Aurie and Delirium can reach them. Only one person left knows, and cannot die: Aurie's daughter.

beats.text: Delirium has a list, written in purple crayon: everyone who ever knew where their brother went.
The first name is an old lawyer in a little desert town, who has kept Destruction's papers for sixty years.
As they cross the street toward his office, the whole old building simply falls down, in a roar of brick and dust.
Delirium holds Aurie's sleeve very tightly. It's him, isn't it, she whispers. He doesn't want to be found.
Aurie does not answer. There are two more names on the list. By the time they reach them, both are already gone.
Delirium crosses them out, very slowly. The crayon breaks.
Aurie drives until the road runs out, at the top of a cliff above a dark blue sea, and stops the car.
There is one person left who knew him, she says. Someone who cannot die, whatever he does.
Who? Delirium asks.
My daughter, says Aurie. She lives in a cave on a Greek island. I have not spoken to her in three thousand years.

choices.text: Then I will go to Orphea.

aftermath.text: Delirium claps her hands. A boat! she says. We have to go in a boat. Please.

6.2o.title: The Song of Orphea
6.2o.recap: Aurie's daughter Orphea lost her bride Eurydice, went down to the dead to bring her back, and looked back. Aurie refused to help her, and told her she was dead to her.

beats.text: Once, Aurie and the Muse Calliope had a daughter. Orphea, whose songs could make the stones weep.
She loved a dancer called Eurydice. On their wedding day, in an olive grove full of music, Aurie came, and even smiled.
That same afternoon, Eurydice ran laughing into the long grass, and stepped on a snake, and died.
Orphea came to her mother's throne, and knelt, and begged her to bring her bride back.
Aurie told her the dead belong to her sister, and refused. She was not cruel. She was correct. To her, that was the same thing.
So Orphea went down alone, into the land of the dead, and stood before its king and queen, and sang.
She sang so well that the rulers of the dead wept, and let Eurydice follow her home, on one condition: she must not look back.
At the very last step, with the daylight on her face, she looked back. And Eurydice faded like breath on a mirror.
Later, the wild women of the hills found her alone, and tore her apart. Her lyre floated down the river to the sea, still playing.
Only her head survived, and it cannot die. Aurie told her she was dead to her, and never went to see her again.
In the boat, Delirium is quiet for a long time. Then she takes her sister's hand, and does not let go.

fin-dream.title: The Last Dream
fin-dream.recap: On the night of the wake, everyone who loved Aurie dreamed the same dream, and in it she spoke to the new Dream one last time.

beats.text: That night, everyone at the wake falls asleep at the same moment, and dreams the same dream.
In it, the throne room of the Dreaming is full of light. And Aurie is there, one last time, as a memory the Dreaming is not ready to let go of.
Daniel, the new Dream, is waiting for her. He has her memories, all of them. He is not her.

canon: This is the last scene of Aurie's story. Aurie, Dream of the Endless, has died and been succeeded by Daniel, Lyta Hall's son, who has become the new Dream: white-haired, robed in white, gentle and grave. He carries Aurie's memories but is a different person.
On the night of her wake, everyone who loved her dreams one shared dream, and in it Aurie's last echo meets Daniel in the throne room. It is a farewell and a passing of the crown.
Daniel is kind, a little afraid of the task, and moved to meet her. He asks what she wants him to remember, and how to be Dream without becoming as lonely as she was.
Daniel always speaks warmly of Lucienne, Matthew and the people of the Dreaming, and promises to look after them.
conversation.opening: You're here. I wasn't sure the Dreaming would let me see you. I have all your memories, you know. Every one. But I don't know how you carried them. How do I do this?
possibilities: She gives him advice: he listens closely and repeats it back, as if writing it down.
She apologises for what was done to his mother: he says Lyta forgave her, in the end, or almost.
She asks him to look after Lucienne and Matthew: he says they are already looking after him.
She tells him she is afraid: he says the Dreaming is not afraid of her any more, and neither is he.
suggestions: Look after Lucienne. She will pretend she doesn't need it.
Were you afraid, when you woke?
I'm sorry about your mother.

exits.fin-dream.KIND: Aurie's last gift to him: be kinder than she was.
exits.fin-dream.WORD: Aurie's last gift to him: keep your word, even when it costs you.
exits.fin-dream.LOVE: Aurie's last gift to him: let them love you.

choices.text: Be kinder than I was. It is not weakness. I learned that too late.

aftermath.text: Daniel nods, and does not argue. Then the dream ends, and everyone at the wake wakes at once, and every one of them is crying, and none of them is sad.

choices.text: Keep your word, even when it costs you everything. Especially then.

aftermath.text: Daniel promises. Then the dream ends, and everyone at the wake wakes at once, and every one of them is crying, and none of them is sad.

choices.text: Let them love you. I never let anyone close enough. Don't make my mistake.

aftermath.text: Daniel smiles, and it is not her smile, but it is close. Then the dream ends, and everyone at the wake wakes at once, and every one of them is crying, and none of them is sad.

fin-hob.title: Sunday Mourning
fin-hob.recap: Years later, Death sat down at Hob Gadling's table, and asked him if he was ready.

beats.text: Hob Gadling comes to the White Horse every year now, on the same day, and buys two pints.
He raises one to the empty chair. To my friend, he says, to anyone who will listen.
He never did hear her say the word. He buys her a pint anyway.
One year, the chair is not empty. A young woman in black, with a silver ankh at her throat, sits down across from him.
Hello, Hob, says Death. My sister asked me to look in on you. Do you want to come with me?
Hob thinks about it for a long time. Then he grins like a boy. Not yet, he says. Life's too good. Ask me again in a hundred years.
Death laughs. She would have liked that, she says. She would have liked that very much.

fin-tempest.title: The Tempest
fin-tempest.recap: Will Shaxberd wrote his last play for the Queen of Dreams: a magician who gives up his power.

beats.text: Long ago, Will Shaxberd made a bargain with the Queen of Dreams: the gift of telling stories, in return for two plays.
The first was about kings and fairies. The second is the last play he will ever write.
It is about an island, and a magician who rules it, and who at the very end breaks his staff, and drowns his book, and gives his power away.
Why that story? he asked her. Because I will never be able to do it, she said. Someone should.
She was wrong. In the end, she did.

fin-walk.title: Hand in Hand
fin-walk.recap: Somewhere past the end of every story, two sisters walk together down a road of light.

beats.text: And somewhere past the end of every story, two sisters walk together down a long road of light.
One of them wears black, and has finally stopped being afraid.
Behind them, in the Dreaming, a new lord in white is being kind to a frightened dream.
Behind them, in the Dreaming, a new lord in white keeps a promise that costs him something.
Behind them, in the Dreaming, a new lord in white lets a raven fall asleep on his shoulder.

beats.card: Specially prepared and programmed for Charmaine Lim

beats.text: The End of The Sandman.
Three more doors are waiting in the Library.

6.2p.title: The Youngest
6.2p.recap: Delirium, the youngest of the Endless, asked her family to help her find their lost brother. Only Aurie listened.

beats.text: Far away, in a realm of colours that have no names, the youngest of the Endless is missing someone.
Delirium was Delight, once, before something happened that nobody talks about. Her brother Destruction used to hold her hand when the colours got too loud.
Three hundred years ago he walked out of his realm and never came back. Today, for no reason she can explain, she has decided to find him.
She goes first to Desire, who laughs at her, and tells her their brother is better off lost.
Then to Despair, who does not look up from her mirrors, and says nothing at all.
So Delirium comes to the Dreaming, skipping through the gates of horn and ivory, trailing little coloured fish through the air.
Lucienne opens the palace door, and is very polite to the fish.
Aurie looks up from her throne, and her youngest sister runs to her across the hall.

canon: Delirium, the youngest of the Endless, who was once Delight, has come to the Dreaming to ask Aurie to help her find their brother Destruction, who abandoned his realm three hundred years ago.
Desire laughed at her and Despair ignored her. Aurie is her last hope, and she is frightened that Aurie will say no too.
Delirium talks in bright, scattered, odd images, jumping between thoughts, but what she wants is clear: her big brother back, and someone to go with her.
If Aurie agrees, Delirium is overjoyed. If Aurie refuses, Delirium does not argue; she goes very small and quiet and leaves.
conversation.opening: Sister! Your hall is all made of night again, I like it. I need... I need to find our brother. The big one, with the red beard, who left. Desire laughed. Despair did that thing with her face. You won't laugh. Will you?
possibilities: She asks why now: Delirium says because yesterday she dreamed of his hands and they were empty.
She is gentle: Delirium's fish turn gold and she starts to hope.
She is cold or dismissive: the fish go grey and Delirium's voice goes very small.
She asks what Destruction would want: Delirium says he would want someone to ask.
suggestions: Why now, little sister?
What makes you think he wants to be found?
Tell me about the fish.

exits.6.2p.YES: Aurie agrees to help Delirium find their brother.

choices.text: Yes. I'll help you find him.

aftermath.text: Delirium throws her arms around her sister. Every fish in the hall turns gold at once.

choices.text: No. He left. Let him stay lost.

aftermath.text: Delirium does not argue. She goes very small and very quiet, and walks out, and her fish follow her, grey.

6.2q.title: Second Thoughts
6.2q.recap: Aurie refused Delirium, then changed her mind and went after her.

beats.text: The hall is very quiet after she has gone. One grey fish is still circling the throne, lost.
A raven on the back of the throne clears his throat. Boss. She's your sister, he says.
Lucienne picks up a single grey scale from the floor, and puts it on the arm of the throne, and says nothing.
Aurie sits with it for a long time. Then she stands, and goes after her sister.
She finds Delirium on the palace steps, drawing sad faces in the sand. I'm sorry, Aurie says. I'll come.

6.2s.title: The Wine-Dark Sea
6.2s.recap: Aurie and Delirium crossed the Aegean in a fisherman's boat, and Aurie told her sister about the daughter she had abandoned.

beats.text: They leave the car on the cliff and take a fisherman's boat, because Delirium wants to, and because Aurie is in no hurry to arrive.
Delirium trails her hand in the water. Little coloured fish follow it, and after a while, some real ones too.
You have a daughter, Delirium says. You never said.
No, says Aurie. I didn't.
And then, because the sea is very wide and her sister is still waiting, she tells her.

6.5d.title: The Only Dream
6.5d.recap: Before paying her price, Orphea asked her mother to walk into her dream. Aurie saw her daughter whole again, the wild women's torches, and Eurydice waiting across a dark river.

beats.text: At dusk, Aurie rows back across the strait alone, as she promised.
Orphea is waiting. The old priestess has gone outside. She knows what is coming.
Before you do it, Orphea says, come into my dream. Just once. I want you to see what you are giving me.
Aurie has walked into more dreams than there are stars. She has never once walked into her daughter's.
And there she is, whole again, on a moonlit beach in Thrace, barefoot in the surf, singing.
In her dream she is twenty-four forever, and the sea still knows all her songs.
Then the torches come over the hill, as they do every night of her dream: the wild women of the hills, wine-mad, crowned with ivy, singing a different song.
Orphea does not run. She never ran. She keeps singing, louder, until the torchlight reaches her and the whole dream burns white.
And then it changes, as it always does: a black river under no moon, and on the far bank, a woman in yellow, holding up a lamp.
Every night for three thousand years, Orphea has dreamed her way to this river. Every night, she wakes before she can cross.
She is standing beside her mother now, on the near bank, looking at the light.

canon: This is Orphea's own dream, the only dream she has had for three thousand years: a moonlit Thracian shore, the night the wild women killed her, and then a dark river with Eurydice waiting on the far bank with a lamp. She always wakes before she can cross.
In her dream Orphea is whole: a beautiful young woman, barefoot, in her white chiton, her lyre on her back. She is calmer and braver here than in the cave, and franker.
She brought her mother here so that Aurie would understand what she is asking for: not death as an ending, but the chance to finally cross this river.
She may ask the question she has carried for three thousand years: why her mother would not help her then. She forgave her long ago, but she has never heard the answer.
If Aurie apologised to her in the cave (flag SORRY_ORPHEUS), she says so: it was the first time her mother had ever said it.
Nothing is decided here. When the talk ends, Aurie wakes in the cave and must still choose.
conversation.opening: You see her? Every night she holds up that lamp, and every night I wake before my feet touch the water. Tell me the truth, Mother. Why wouldn't you help me, back then?
possibilities: Aurie explains the law, the dead belong to Death: Orphea says she knows, and that it was never the law she needed, it was her mother.
Aurie admits she was wrong, or afraid: Orphea is silent, then takes her hand.
Aurie asks about Eurydice: Orphea tells her how Eurydice laughed, and that she has not heard that laugh in three thousand years.
Aurie is cold: Orphea says, quietly, that this is why she wanted her to see it.
suggestions: Tell me about her.
I was afraid, Orphea. Not of the law. Of losing you.
The dead belong to my sister. That was the law.

exits.6.5d.HOLD: Aurie holds her daughter, there on the riverbank.
exits.6.5d.WAKE: Aurie leaves the dream and wakes in the cave.

choices.text: (Hold her.)

aftermath.text: For the first time in three thousand years, the Queen of Dreams holds her daughter. On the far bank, the lamp burns a little brighter.

choices.text: I've seen enough. Wake up, Orphea.

aftermath.text: The river, the lamp and the shore fold away like a page turning.
